name: Ambe Sasam

ingredients.name: firm ripe mango flesh, cut into chunks

steps: Choose mangoes that are ripe and sweet but still firm enough to cut. Peel, cut the flesh into generous chunks, and collect any juice in the serving bowl.

Dry-toast 6 g of the dried red chilies for 1 minute. Grind them with coconut, 5 g mustard seeds and 120 ml water to a smooth, thick paste; stop as soon as it is smooth so the mustard stays pleasantly sharp rather than bitter.

Fold the coconut-mustard paste, jaggery and salt through the mango chunks. Add the remaining 60 ml water a little at a time to make a coating sauce, not a thin soup. Taste and balance sweetness against mustard heat.
Warm coconut oil in a small pan. Crackle the remaining 3 g mustard seeds, then fry the remaining 2 g dried chili and curry leaves for 20 seconds. Pour over the mango mixture.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then serve at room temperature alongside rice and a mild dal. Do not simmer the ripe mango; its fresh texture is part of this Konkani dish.
tips: Use sweet, fragrant ripe mango, not sour green mango. If mangoes are very sweet, reduce jaggery after tasting; grind mustard briefly to avoid bitterness.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
